prompt_text: I am planning a trip. Should I book on Airbnb, Vrbo, or Booking.com, and how do I find a good host?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: it depends on what you need. Airbnb, Vrbo and Booking.com each have strengths. Choose based on type of trip (hotel vs whole home vs unique stay), flexibility, fees, and how much host interaction you want. Below are quick comparisons and practical, step-by-step tips to find a good host and a safe booking.

Which platform to pick (quick guide)
- Airbnb — best for unique stays, private rooms, entire homes, and local “host” experiences. Big selection of entire homes and long-stay options. Strong guest protections but service fees can be high.
- Vrbo — focused on whole-home vacation rentals (good for families/groups). Generally fewer shared/room listings than Airbnb. Often better for larger properties and family-oriented amenities.
- Booking.com — strongest if you want hotels, aparthotels, or instant-book apartments with flexible cancellation. Good for last-minute bookings and business travel; many properties accept free cancellation and pay-on-arrival. Listings vary in quality because it aggregates hotels and private rentals.
- When to choose which:
  - Family or large group whole-house rental → Vrbo or Airbnb
  - Short hotel-like stay or maximum flexibility/cancellation → Booking.com
  - Looking for quirky/unique home or a host who offers local tips → Airbnb
  - Want many instant-book options and last-minute availability → Booking.com

How to find a good host (step-by-step)
1. Filter and narrow:
   - Select “Entire place” if you need privacy.
   - Set essentials (Wi‑Fi speed, kitchen, washer, AC, parking) and number of beds/bathrooms.
   - Prefer “Instant Book” for fast confirmation or filter for “Superhost/Premier Host” for established hosts.
2. Sort and read reviews:
   - Sort by “review score” or “most relevant”.
   - Read recent reviews (last 6–12 months) — look for mentions of cleanliness, accuracy of listing, communication, neighborhood noise, and check-in process.
   - Pay attention to patterns (repeated praise or repeated complaints).
3. Check the listing details carefully:
   - Compare photos to the description; make sure room counts, bed types, and amenities match.
   - Confirm total price (cleaning fee, service fee, local taxes, security deposit) — platforms sometimes show different totals at different checkout stages.
   - Look for house manual, check-in instructions, and explicit rules (pets, smoking, extra guests).
4. Inspect the host’s profile:
   - Look for ID verification, number of listings, response rate/time, and length of time hosting.
   - “Superhost” (Airbnb)/“Premier Host” (Vrbo) or high review counts are good signals of reliability.
5. Message the host before booking (or immediately after booking):
   - Ask clarifying questions (sample template below). Good hosts respond promptly, politely, and provide helpful details.
6. Watch for red flags:
   - Poor or generic photos, many negative or mixed recent reviews, host avoids direct answers, requests to pay outside the platform, or unclear check-in instructions.
7. Book and protect:
   - Pay only via the platform. Keep communication on the platform. Confirm cancellation policy and refund rules.
   - Consider travel insurance for cancellation or damage coverage if needed.

Red flags to avoid
- Host asks to pay outside the platform or send a wire transfer.
- No recent reviews (or many reviews older than a year).
- Vague or contradictory listing details (amenities listed in text but not visible in photos).
- Last-minute listing price drastically lower than similar properties in the area.
- Host refuses to provide ID or gives evasive answers about the property or check-in.

Sample message to send a prospective host
Hi — I’m [Your Name]. I’m traveling with [number and relationship, e.g., 2 adults + 1 child] from [dates]. I have a few quick questions before booking:
1) Is the price quoted the total (including cleaning/taxes/security deposit)?  
2) What is the check-in process and earliest arrival time? Is self check-in available?  
3) Is parking available? Any extra cost?  
4) How reliable is the Wi‑Fi? (I’ll be working remotely / need streaming)  
5) Are linens and towels provided? Is there a washing machine?  
6) Any house rules we should know about (quiet hours, smoking, guests)?  
Thanks — we’re tidy and respectful guests. Looking forward to your reply.

Negotiation and discounts
- Ask for weekly/monthly discounts (many hosts offer them).
- For off-season and last-minute stays you can politely request a lower price—do so through the platform message and be reasonable.
- Avoid offers to pay outside the platform — that voids platform protections.

Safety and payment warnings
- Always pay through the platform. Never wire money or pay cash to a host asking you to bypass the site.
- Keep all messages on the platform in case you need support.
- Check cancellation policy and whether the host or platform provides refunds for travel disruptions.
- Read platform protections (Airbnb’s refund policy, Vrbo/Booking.com terms) — they differ in details.

One-page checklist before booking
- Verified ID & host status (Superhost/Premier Host)
- Many recent positive reviews (check for consistency)
- Clear, matching photos and accurate description
- Total price shown (no hidden fees)
- Clear check-in instructions and parking info
- Host answers pre-booking questions promptly
- Acceptable cancellation policy for your needs
- Payment through the platform only

If you tell me your destination, travel dates, group size, and priorities (price, location, flexibility, whole place vs room, work-from-home needs), I can give a tailored recommendation and sample listings search strategy.
